solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Draw attention to grass wearing thin

indicators.note: the grass wears the thin word like a coat, so the word for thin wraps around it

parts.note: slight means thin or slender
pot is slang for cannabis, also called grass

explanation.surface: A lawn gone patchy and threadbare draws the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' makes the thin word clothe the grass; 'grass' here is the drug, not the lawn the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight or draw attention to something is to put a spotlight on it, used as a verb.

clue.text: Letter-writer vindictive about paper's leader

indicators.note: the word for vindictive goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: penal means punitive, inflicting punishment, hence vindictive

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of paper's

explanation.surface: A spiteful correspondent takes aim at a newspaper editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper's leader' looks like a newspaper's editorial, but it is only its first letter, P, which 'about' puts inside PENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent one exchanges letters with, often a stranger abroad, is a classic letter-writer.

clue.text: Mobile home kept in large storage unit criminals organised

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are held within the abbreviation for the storage unit

parts.note: TB is a terabyte, a large unit of computer storage

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters of home move around

explanation.surface: A caravan is stashed in a big warehouse by an organised gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile home' reads as a caravan, but 'Mobile' signals rearranging the next word, and 'kept in' places the result inside a terabyte's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common name for organised crime as a collective, gangsters and racketeers.

clue.text: Half of bitter in pub could represent one's wages?

definitions.text: Half of bitter in pub could represent one's wages?

indicators.note: the half word is placed inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the second half of the word bitter is taken

explanation.surface: A trainee's pay might stretch to half a pint of beer at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes the back half of 'bitter' and 'in' places it in the pub. The whole clue jokes that a trainee's wages might buy only half a bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee doing work experience, often poorly paid or unpaid, is so meagrely rewarded that half a beer might be their pay.

clue.text: Regular held up European organisation note: 'Humbug!'

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: EU is the European Union
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
bah is an exclamation like humbug

explanation.surface: A regular complains that a European body has delayed things, scoffing 'Humbug!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns EU + TI + BAH backwards, upwards in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loan word for a frequent visitor to a place, such as a regular at a bar.

clue.text: Torn muscle in a strapping

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A burly athlete has suffered a torn muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torn' rearranges MUSCLEINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapping describes a big, sturdy, manly build, which is what this adjective conveys.

clue.text: Rodents going over where one serves food, right?

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the word for rodents is turned around

parts.note: rats are rodents
a board is a table at which food is served, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Rats scuttle over the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns RATS into STAR. The question mark flags that the definition is a nautical sense of 'right'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the right-hand side looking forward is called by this name.

clue.text: Site raved about in hype

indicators.note: about here means around and astray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A website got rave reviews amid all the hype.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SITERAVED.
explanation.definitionFit: To hype something is to promote or publicise it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Rocked around clock once exhausted?

parts.note: was means once upon a time, in the past
a Ted, a Teddy boy, was the youth of the 1950s who rocked to Rock Around the Clock

explanation.surface: Someone who danced all night to Bill Haley is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress who danced to the hit Rock Around the Clock; split 3,3 the answer reads 'was a Ted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn out, drained or spent is a sense of the adjective; slang also has it for very drunk.

clue.text: Number taken in by sluggish university — happen it should be blown up

indicators.note: the letter for number is taken inside the word for sluggish

parts.note: inert means inactive, sluggish
to be is to happen or take place, as in 'what will be'

explanation.surface: A slow student gets a number, and a northern 'happen' shrugs at the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts N inside INERT. 'Happen' is also northern English dialect for 'perhaps', which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable rubber ring inside a tyre is something to be pumped up with air.

clue.text: Build up outstanding vintage for investment

indicators.note: invest means to enclose or lay siege to, so one word is surrounded by the other

parts.note: ace means excellent, outstanding
cru is a wine of a particular vineyard or grade, a vintage

explanation.surface: A fine wine put away as an investment will appreciate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for investment' uses 'invest' in its old military sense of besieging or surrounding, not the financial one the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate, or grow over time like interest, is to build up.

clue.text: Choice tofu I rave about

indicators.note: about means around and astray, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vegetarian enthuses about their preferred bean curd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TOFUIRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A preferred selection, the pick of the bunch, is one's choice; noun for noun.

clue.text: Nut missing north departs street, more or less

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so letters are taken out of the word for nut

parts.note: an almond is a nut
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone loses a nut, heads off and leaves the street, roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' strips N and D from ALMOND, leaving ALMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly or very nearly is the adverbial sense, much the same as more or less.

clue.text: Unclear about total by sea in France in June?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for unclear is reversed

parts.note: dim means faint or unclear
a sum is a total
mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: Someone is hazy about the full cost of a holiday by the French seaside in June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DIM into MID. The question mark admits that the definition is a description, true only in the northern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The period around the summer solstice, 21 June in the north, is the middle of summer.

clue.text: School head covered in piercings may constitute a feature

parts.note: a nozzle, like a shower head or sprinkler rose, is a head full of holes

explanation.surface: A head teacher with facial piercings has a distinctive look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head covered in piercings' looks like a pierced pupil, but it describes a perforated spout.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for the nose, which is a facial feature, especially a big one.

clue.text: Duvet slid off — this restricts breathing?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duvet slipped off the bed, perhaps helping a sleeper breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges DUVETSLID. The question mark covers a playful definition: a whirl of grit would choke anyone in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small whirlwind that lifts dust and sand across dry land would make it hard to draw breath.

clue.text: Host waves

definitions.meaning: a host can mean a great multitude
the waves, poetically, are the ocean itself

explanation.surface: A hostess greets her guests with a wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast crowd is figuratively an ocean of people, and the briny deep is where waves roll.

clue.text: Darn waste — but there's no time

indicators.note: there being no time means the word for time is taken out

parts.note: sewage is waste matter
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone curses wasted effort with no time left to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darn' seems an exclamation, but it is a verb for mending. Without AGE, SEWAGE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To darn a sock is to mend it with needle and thread, a kind of stitching.

clue.text: Matilda occasionally providing help

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: A girl called Matilda lends a hand now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of Matilda.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance or support is a direct noun synonym for help.

clue.text: New evidence will hold key, one is first to admit

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed at the front of everything else

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word for evidence holds the key letter inside it

parts.note: a clue is a piece of evidence in a mystery
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: Fresh evidence will contain the key, and someone must be first to confess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will hold' puts D inside CLUE; 'is first' puts I before N and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone into a group is to let them in, which is to count them in as part of it.

clue.text: Guts shown by local while crossing road

parts.note: the local is British slang for one's nearby pub, an inn

indicators.note: the word for while goes across the road abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'

explanation.surface: Someone shows real courage dashing across the road from the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' suggests courage, but it is the entrails. 'crossing' has the word for while straddle the road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The internal organs of the body, the bowels and entrails, are the guts.

clue.text: Take the plunge midweek

definitions.meaning: to take the plunge is an idiom for getting married
the abbreviation for the day in the middle of the working week, Wednesday

explanation.surface: A couple decide to get married in the middle of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying is the idiomatic plunge, and the three-letter short form names Wednesday, the middle of the week.

clue.text: Removal firm appears after time

indicators.note: the word for firm comes after the word for time in the answer

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means firm, steady

explanation.surface: A removals company turns up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removal firm' reads as a removal company, but the definition is just 'Removal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of rubbing out or deleting something is a removal of it.

clue.text: Within reason a talent for composition

indicators.note: within means the answer lies inside the run of words reason a talent

explanation.surface: A reasonable gift for writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within' points to letters running across 'reason a talent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of instrumental music in several movements is a type of musical composition.

clue.text: Having stirred kippers, present them with this?

definitions.text: Having stirred kippers, present them with this?

parts.words: Having stirred kippers, present them with this?
parts.note: kippers are slang for sleepers; once they have been stirred awake, a breakfast item can be set before them

explanation.surface: Cooking smoked herring, you serve it in some container.
explanation.walkthrough: Kippers are smoked herrings, a British breakfast fish, but here they are people who kip (sleep); once roused they are served a boiled breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A small holder for a boiled egg is laid at the breakfast table for those just woken.

clue.text: Secure with string

definitions.meaning: secure as an adjective means firm and steady
a string is a group of racehorses kept by one owner or trainer

explanation.surface: Fasten something with a piece of cord.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly fixed means steady and secure, and the yard housing a trainer's horses is the name of that string.

clue.text: Expose humorist better

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
a wit is a humorist

explanation.surface: Unmasking a comedian beats him at his own game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here, meaning to get the better of.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone by cleverness is to outsmart them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Buffet e.g. mutton, including a vegetable

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the single letter
to buffet is to batter and knock about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A buffet serving mutton with some greens on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a spread of food, but it signals rearranging EGMUTTON; 'including' adds A.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat pea pod eaten whole, a French-named vegetable, also called the snow pea.

clue.text: Top group putting on look that's close to stern

indicators.note: the band puts on the look, as one puts on clothes, and so sits inside it

parts.note: mien is a person's look or bearing
ZZ Top is a rock band, so the Top group gives ZZ

explanation.surface: A leading band adopts a severe expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top group' reads as a chart-topping band; it is the band ZZ Top, giving ZZ. 'stern' looks like 'severe' but is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftermost mast of a sailing ship, just ahead of the stern, has this name.

clue.text: Entertaining party piece with a knockout to deliver?

parts.note: a punch is a blow that can be a knockout
to bowl is to deliver the ball in cricket

explanation.surface: A party trick that delivers a real knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining party piece' sounds like a turn, but it is a bowl of drink for entertaining guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bowl of mixed drink set out when hosting guests is an item for a party.

clue.text: Engineer clear about one creation that is 'long in shape, but short in duration'

definitions.text: creation that is 'long in shape, but short in duration'

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the letter for one
to engineer is to contrive or arrange, so the letters of clear are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A designer explains something oblong that will not last long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a person but signals rearranging CLEAR; 'about' wraps it round I. The quoted definition is Chambers' famous whimsical entry for this pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger-shaped choux pastry is long in shape and, being delicious, soon eaten.

clue.text: Voila drunk hero types

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and staggering, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy hero shows off with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges HEROTYPES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjuror's exclamations announcing a trick's sudden result, there you are.
